title: Standards, batch records and staying approved
course_title: Business Registration & Compliance for Product Makers: NAFDAC, SON and Safe Production

say: Standards, batch records, and staying approved.
This is the video for module three of Business Registration and Compliance: growth, traceability and renewals.
Approval is the start, not the finish. Makers of textiles, leather goods, candles or paving stones may need the Standards Organisation of Nigeria, SON, not NAFDAC.

say: As you grow, products travel to shops and homes you never see. Traceability means that from any one pack, you can find when it was made, from what, by whom, and where the rest of that batch went.

say: And most approved makers fall out of compliance not by fraud, but by forgetting a date.

say: MANCAP is SON's certification scheme for locally made products, against Nigerian Industrial Standards.
For example, Bola in Abeokuta dyes adire, and a retail chain wants to stock it. She visits the SON state office and writes down the officer's name and answer.

panel.heading: The MANCAP steps
items: Contact a SON state office or apply online
CAC certificate, lab test report, payment
At least two quarterly inspections
Certificate and logo with a unique number
Quarterly checks; recertify after three years

say: She submits her CAC certificate, a test report from a SON or IPAN-accredited laboratory, and proof of payment.

panel.heading: The MANCAP steps
items: Contact a SON state office or apply online
CAC certificate, lab test report, payment
At least two quarterly inspections
Certificate and logo with a unique number
Quarterly checks; recertify after three years

say: SON inspects at least twice, a quarter apart, before certifying. So Bola expects at least six months, and asks about the fast track for small businesses.

say: She then receives the certificate and logo. It is valid for three years, with inspections every quarter, so her records must stay alive, not be prepared once.

panel.rule: Ask SON before you spend, and keep the answer in writing.

say: A batch is everything made from one mix. Give it a code and print it on every pack. For example, CC-260312-02 means chin-chin, made on 12 March 2026, second batch that day.

panel.heading: A batch number that means something
items: Code: product, date, batch of the day
Batch record: ingredients, suppliers, times
Distribution record: who got which batch
Retained samples kept past best-before

say: The batch record lists each ingredient, its supplier and expiry date, key times and temperatures, and who checked the batch.

say: A distribution record lists the date, buyer, batch and quantity. And keep retained samples from each batch until after the best-before date.

say: For example, Ngozi in Port Harcourt gets a call. A pack of chin-chin smells rancid. She logs the complaint and the code, CC-260312-02, and asks the shop to keep the pack.

panel.heading: A complaint and a quiet recall
items: Log the complaint and pack code
Stop selling that batch at once
Check retained sample and batch record
Find every buyer in the distribution record
Remove, replace, fix the cause, report

say: She stops selling that batch immediately.

say: Her distribution record shows 120 packs: 40 to this shop, 50 to a supermarket, and 30 sold on WhatsApp to 9 customers.

say: She removes and replaces the batch, contacts all 9 customers, goes back to her old oil supplier, and reports to NAFDAC. Within two days, it is done.
If a complaint suggests illness, a foreign object or an allergic reaction, stop sales at once, keep the evidence, encourage the person to see a health worker, and contact NAFDAC.

say: Train workers in three steps. Show: fill one batch record yourself while they watch.

panel.heading: Teach records: show, do, check

cards.d: Fill one batch record yourself while the worker watches, explaining why each line matters.
The worker fills the next record while you watch, and you correct gently on the spot.
For the next five batches, the worker fills it alone and you check and sign each one.

say: Do: they fill the next one while you watch and correct gently.

say: Check: for five batches, they fill it alone and you sign each one.
Explain the why. A worker who knows the batch code saves the business in a recall will not skip it on a busy Saturday.

say: For example, Zainab collected her listing certificate on 10 February 2026. It expires two years later, so she sets a renewal alarm for 10 August 2027, six months early.
She sets fumigation reminders a month before each due date, checks medical tests for every new worker, and reviews her file on the first Monday of every month.
Before changing a formula, pack, label claim, address or product, ask NAFDAC or SON first.

panel.heading: Your compliance calendar
items: Listing certificate: remind 6 months before
MANCAP: each quarter, and before expiry
Fumigation: one month before due
Medical tests: at hiring and when due
Compliance review: first Monday monthly

say: To remember. Ask SON whether your product needs MANCAP. Put a batch code on every pack. Batch and distribution records make a recall small and quick.
When safety is in doubt, stop sales first. And put every expiry date in a calendar with early reminders.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Ask SON whether your product needs MANCAP
Product-date-number codes on every pack
Batch and distribution records shrink recalls
When safety is in doubt, stop sales first
Every expiry date in a calendar, early

say: Now practise. Build your buyer pack, set up batch, distribution and complaint records for your next batch, and write your compliance calendar and 90-day plan.
